parole.significato: A ghost or spirit, often malevolent, in Polynesian mythology.
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Polynesian language, from Proto-Polynesian *qaitu.

parole.significato: Non-taboo; serving to replace a taboo name or term.
parole.testo: From the Polynesian term noa, e.g. Hawaiian noa (“free of taboo”).

parole.significato: An image made on a body part, usually the skin with ink and a needle.
parole.testo: From earlier tattaow, tattow, a borrowing from a Polynesian language, e.g. Samoan tatau (“tattoo; to tap, to strike”).

parole.significato: A good luck plant (Cordyline fruticosa), an evergreen shrub.
parole.testo: From a Polynesian language, related to Hawaiian kī.
